evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/AppRoutes.tsx:37 — AppRoutes mounts every feature group directly; there is NO top-level auth guard, so authentication is enforced per-route by <ProtectedRoute> inside each group.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/faults.tsx:564 faultRoutes() — 5 routes (/faults, /faults/new, /faults/reports, /faults/:faultId, /faults/:faultId/edit) mounted with NO <ProtectedRoute> wrapper (file does not import ProtectedRoute); same gap in announcements.tsx, disputes.tsx, messaging.tsx, neighbors.tsx, community.tsx (grep: 0 ProtectedRoute, 0 isAuthenticated/Navigate-to-login/setReturnUrl in all six).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/documents.tsx + voting.tsx + core.tsx + meters.tsx + reports.tsx — sibling groups DO wrap their routes in <ProtectedRoute>, confirming the pattern the six unguarded groups deviate from.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx:1 — ProtectedRoute is what redirects unauthenticated users to /login and calls setReturnUrl(); routes not wrapped in it neither redirect nor store the return URL.
signals.failure_scenario: A logged-out user deep-links to /disputes (or /faults, /messages, /neighbors, /community, /announcements). Because these route groups are not wrapped in <ProtectedRoute>, the app does not redirect to /login and does not store the return URL. The protected page mounts, its API calls 401, and the 401 interceptor's logout() clears state without navigating — leaving the user on a broken/empty page instead of the login screen, and breaking the post-login return-to-page flow that guarded routes (documents, voting, settings) provide. Data is still protected by the backend, so this is a client-side auth-guard consistency + UX defect, not a data-leak bypass.
signals.summary: Six ppt-web route groups (faults, announcements, disputes, messaging, neighbors, community) mount authenticated pages without <ProtectedRoute>, so unauthenticated deep-links neither redirect to /login nor store a return URL — inconsistent with sibling groups that do.
signals.short_summary: 6 route groups mount authed pages without ProtectedRoute

signals.failure_scenario: An uncaught runtime/typing error (e.g. "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x')") reaches parseApiError; its raw English technical message is rendered to the end user of a 4-locale app (sk/cs/de/en), bypassing the i18n error catalogue and potentially disclosing internal details in the UI.
signals.summary: errorHandler surfaces raw JS Error / backend `message` strings directly to users, bypassing the i18n error catalogue used elsewhere in the same module.
signals.short_summary: errorHandler leaks raw untranslated error.message to users
